data.summary: Single merged reviewer at fast tier over the aggregate diff. The read path is clean and correctly layered, core/verify honours the ImageBitmap single-file rule, and conventions are genuinely clean (no literal colours, no inline TextStyle, no raw dp at a call site). The original verdict was request-changes on COR-1, a real cancellation defect the 1170-test suite structurally could not catch. All seven findings were fixed in commit f789015 and the verdict is revised to approve-with-nits.

findings.summary: Cancelling verifyJob did not stop the run: resultLauncher caught Throwable and swallowed CancellationException, and Orbit's reduce is a non-suspending StateFlow.update with no cancellation check.
findings.failureScenario: Verify parks in the ~2.7s dump; the user presses Back-to-live; exitVerify cancels and clears, then the cancelled run resumes, sees a null snapshot and calls abortVerify(Disconnected) - throwing the user back into the Verify stage reading 'The device went away' for a device that never dropped. On a real device adb's blocking read is not interruptible at all, so the dump succeeds, the abandoned run walks steps 5-7, republishes two full-frame bitmaps after the exit that existed to drop them, and writes Verified to the database for a run the user abandoned.
findings.note: Fixed at both layers. The red-then-green proof is the important part: once the fakes were made to swallow cancellation the way production did, two PRE-EXISTING tests failed - they had been passing on the fakes' better manners.

findings.summary: canSendGate was never taught about the Verify stage, so the toolbar Send button and the shortcut it advertises dispatched two different intents.
findings.failureScenario: Freeze a frame, stage two annotations, Verify an old batch, press the shortcut: sendFollowUp overwrites the frozen frame and silently destroys the staged annotations, under a label describing the opposite action. Click the toolbar Send instead and Preparing/Publishing/Failed all render behind the verify stage, invisible.

findings.summary: The stage branched progress-vs-result on frames == null, but the frames publish at the START of Diffing, before any row is computed.
findings.failureScenario: For the whole diff window the panel shows empty frame columns and reads '0 of 0 fixed' with Mark-all-as-verified enabled, asserting a result that does not exist.

findings.summary: deviceLabel was seeded from the live selection and only replaced with the batch's own label after the NoLiveSession abort.
findings.failureScenario: App opened with history and no device selected - the primary NoLiveSession case - renders 'Nothing is streaming from , so there is no fresh frame to compare against.' with a blank where the device name belongs.
findings.note: The fixture hid it too: phone() and sentBatch() both used 'Pixel 8 Pro', so the obvious assertion would have passed against the live name.

findings.summary: regionPx == 0 is the documented no-region-could-be-read sentinel, but the guard treated it as 'too small to measure' and waived the pixel conjunct entirely.
findings.failureScenario: A degenerate or fully-off-frame stored rect yields Fixed on the hierarchy half alone, with provably zero pixel evidence - inverting the very change-evidence correction this spec is built on.

findings.summary: TOUCH_TARGET_ADVISED_DP = 48 duplicated the literal in MeasureFormat.kt with a KDoc pointing at the other copy.
findings.failureScenario: Two copies of a design constant drift apart.

findings.summary: Two consecutive KDoc blocks on FakeUpdateBatchStatus; the first is dead.
findings.failureScenario: A reader edits the block the compiler ignores.

changeRequests.about: COR-1 cancellation reaching a checkpoint, at both the resultLauncher and ViewModel layers
COR-2 gate canSend on verify == null
COR-3/4/5 one-liners plus the two nits

techDebt: ProcessRunner's withTimeoutOrNull choice stays correct after the resultLauncher fix but for the opposite reason - a TimeoutCancellationException would now unwind rather than surface the named timeout prefix the escalation ladder matches on. Comment updated, code deliberately unchanged.
The write-after-abandon path could not be reproduced in-test (the zombie run unwinds at the diff before reaching the status write); the guard is in, but the evidence stops at the republished pixels.
MET-3's false-positive rate remains unmeasured - no golden corpus.
The end-to-end GUI demo was never walked on a real device.
backlog T-11 still lists the cut four-step progress strip.
data-database-impl's iOS test task is NO-SOURCE, so the DAO test never runs on iOS.

survey.question: COR-1 showed that cancelling verifyJob did not stop a run in production, and the 1170-test suite could not catch it because the fakes propagated cancellation better than production did. How should the PR proceed?
options: Merge now and file them as follow-ups
survey.rationale: COR-1 writes durable wrong database state and breaks the feature's own documented lifecycle contract. COR-5 inverts the change-evidence semantics the whole spec rests on, and COR-3/4 are user-visible one-liners - batching them was one pass over files already open, and the reviewer explicitly allowed it.
